en.text: He grimaced as if memories of his bitter past were crashing like waves inside his head.

en.text: I said that I don't remember having had any toys, and I also don't remember having had any snacks.

original: そして、そういいながら、自分を誘惑した男、戯談のようにいい寄った夫の同僚の一人、手を握った会社の課長、酔って接吻をしようとした親族の男などを、くだけた鏡に写っている記憶のように、きらきらと、閃かせた。

en.text: Then, while saying this, the memories of the men who had seduced her, her husband's colleague who had approached her as if it were a joke, the section chief with whom she had held hands, her relative who she had tried to kiss while she was drunk, shined as if projected upon a broken mirror.

original: そんなにたくさんの文字を記憶できません。

en.text: I can't memorize so many of these letters.

original: このアニメ、子供時代によく見てたんだけど、最終回で主人公がどうなったかの記憶があやふやなんだ。

en.text: I used to watch this anime a lot when I was a kid, but I can't quite remember what happened to the hero in the final episode.

original: お酒を飲んだ後の記憶がすっぽりと抜けているんだよ。どうして俺の部屋に知らないおっさんが寝てるんだ？

en.text: I have absolutely no clue what happened after I got drunk. Why is there some old dude sleeping in my room?

original: 子供の頃どんなおもちゃも持っていたという記憶がない。

en.text: I don't remember having had any toys when I was young.

original: 二度と取り戻せない記憶なんて、寂しい。

en.text: How sad it is to have a memory that you'll never be able to recall again.

original: 人は年をとるにつれて記憶力が悪くなる。

en.text: As we age, our ability to remember gets worse.

original: 彼は驚異的な記憶力を持っていた。

en.text: He had a wonderfully powerful memory.

en.text: Remember me next time.

en.text: Happy people are those who remember only the good things from the past, while unhappy people are those who remember only the opposite.
